premises.text: Developers must buy many devices and hire testers or risk bad App Store reviews
premises.evidence_span: You have to buy a lot of devices. You have to hire a lot of people. And then, if you don't do it, you're probably going to get bad review in the App Store

premises.text: Existing cloud testing asks for unit tests and returns long error logs without the physical device
premises.evidence_span: they present developers with a very long log with a lot of errors

premises.text: NativeTap puts remote real devices on a tablet/desktop so interaction and debugging feel USB-local
premises.evidence_span: it's as if it was USB connected to your computer

premises.text: Efficient multi-device servers, queuing, and racks enable scalable low-cost device access
premises.evidence_span: fewer data centers, fewer servers, and higher gross margins

value.text: Create better apps with greater market reach by testing on real devices affordably
value.evidence_span: you create better apps with greater market reach

secondary_value.text: Save money accessing any device for a fraction of cost
secondary_value.evidence_span: You save money. You can access any device anytime you want for a fraction of cost

causal_links.evidence_span: you don't have to now limit your target group simply because you can't afford to purchase all of those devices
access and interact with any real mobile device just with one tap
one server can support up to 250 devices

notes: Patent I/O tech folded into desk-like access premise. Planned multi-device replication and IoT features folded as extensions of same mechanism.
